newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bankers group sets agenda for annual meeting.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bankers group sets agenda for annual meeting.

text.p: Technology, regulation and mergers are expected to be prime topics at the annual conference of the U.S. Council on International Banking set for the end of October.
"Regulatory issues are always hot topics," said Dan Taylor, president of the council. Risk management is also certain to be on the minds of the 300 senior international bankers, he said.

According to Roy DeCicco, conference chairman and a vice president at Chase Manhattan Corp, a special focus of this year's meeting will be cross border settlement. He said a session at the conference will be devoted to discussion of "continuous link settlement" and other concepts.
DeCicco said in a telephone interview that global payment systems are at a very secure level but at the same time it is recognized that systems are not infallible.
"We have to continue to stay ahead of the curve," he said. "What might be secure today isn't necessarily a secure process a year or two years from now."

He said plans to extend the hours of operation of the Fed wire to 18 hours a day is widely viewed in the industry as a positive move. An earlier start time for Fed wire will bring overlap with the Asian trading day, he noted.

Other speakers at the five-day event include Martin Stein, vice chairman of BankAmerica Corp, who will focus on electronic commerce and the future of banking; Robert Cohen, chief executive officer of Credit Lyonnais Americas, who will discuss the evolution of foreign banking in the U.S.; Patrick Mulloy, chief international consel of the Senate Banking Committee, who will discuss current legislative issues, and Malcolm Burnett, chief operating officer of Marine Midland Bank, whose topic will be financial services in the global marektplace.
The council's meeing is set to begin October 26 at Hilton Head, S.C. and run through October 30.
